newsitem.title: UK: IPE to step up talks with SIMEX on struggling link.
newsitem.headline: IPE to step up talks with SIMEX on struggling link.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) plans to step up talks next month with the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) on ways to boost volume in its struggling Brent crude linkup, IPE chief executive Lynton Jones said on Monday.

The London exchange has pinned its growth in Asia on its 16-month-old Mutual Offset System with SIMEX but it has admitted disappointment with the lack of interest, which it has blamed on marketing and the poor location on the SIMEX trading floor.

Jones said it was becoming apparent that the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) would eventually have its own screen-based trading system, called ACCESS, in Singapore, but he did not view that as a threat.
"I suppose it will only be a matter of time before (NYMEX) gets into Singapore but I don't see WTI (NYMEX crude futures) as a competitor to Brent," Jones told Reuters. "They compliment each other."
"We've been talking about various measures that might be taken and we plan to have more formal negotiations in the month of November," said Jones, who joined the IPE on August 1.

He said the measures were aimed primarily at "ways to increase awareness of the availability of the contract" and include discussions on its own electronic trading system and shorter hours on the IPE for its open outcry trading.

The IPE still has no firm date for the launch of its natural gas forward contract, delayed this year over verification of the physical delivery of gas, but Jones said it still hoped trading will start as soon as possible.

NYMEX Chairman Daniel Rappaport, in London last week for London Metal Exchange Week, said it was pursuing opportunities to install its ACCESS machines in Singapore, but that the SIMEX had not offered any firm commitment to let this happen.
NYMEX has already signed an agreement to hook up the Hong Kong Futures Exchange to its ACCESS system, probably near the end of March 1997.
